C920: Progress Stackable Chair
Product URL: https://www.anchortex.com/products/norix-progress-chair
Manufacturer page: https://norix.com/product/progress-chair/
Spec sheets: C920 Progress Chair, Progress Brochure
Recommended H1 and Subtitle
H1: Norix Progress Molded Stackable Chair – C920
Current H1: Norix Progress - Molded Stackable Chair - Model C920
Subtitle: Passive Ergonomic Stacking Chair with a Flexible Molded Backrest for Staff Areas, Classrooms, and Training Rooms
Current subtitle: Norix Furniture C920 Progress Chair
Revised Product Description
Headings marked [H2] should be set as H2 on the page.
The Norix Progress Stackable Chair is a passive ergonomic chair with a live hinge molded into the backrest, so the back flexes for comfort in both upright and relaxed sitting positions. The one-piece seat shell sits on black powder-coated aluminum legs, and the chairs nest when stacked for compact storage.
The simple design has no nuts, bolts, welds, or rivets to tamper with. Norix recommends the Progress Chair for staff use and monitored programming rooms, such as classrooms, training rooms, offices, and lobbies. It is not suitable for confined areas.
Seat Shell: One-piece, injection-molded high-impact grade copolymer polypropylene, with an anti-static inhibitor added when molded
Flexible Backrest: A live hinge molded into the backrest gives the flexibility needed for long-term comfort
Legs: Black powder-coated aluminum with friction fit foot caps
Tamper Resistant: No nuts, bolts, welds, or rivets
Stackable: The leg shape lets the chairs nest when stacked
Seat Colors: Twilight, Cove, Sand, or Dove
Dimensions: 19.7”W×23.2”D×32”H, with a 17.3” seat height
Weight: 10 lbs
Static Load Testing: Tested to 500 lbs
Performance Standards: ANSI/BIFMA X5.1 2002 General Purpose Office Chairs; ISO 14001:2015
Environmental Certification: GREENGUARD and GREENGUARD Gold
Flammability: Not California Technical Bulletin 133 compliant
Cleaning: Simple Green or a similar cleaner for routine cleaning, and Clorox Clean-Up Cleaner + Bleach for tougher stains; soap and water for the legs
Warranty: 10 year limited replacement warranty
Intended Use: Indoor use only
Available Models and Options
C920 – Progress Chair: Armless stackable chair in Twilight, Cove, Sand, or Dove, 10 lbs
Upholstered Option: The Progress Chair is also available with upholstery, in 8 Norix fabric grades
Installation and Options
No assembly is required.
[H2] Applications
The Norix Progress Chair suits supervised areas where staff and visitors need comfortable seating that stacks away when the room is cleared.
Typical applications include:
Staff offices, break rooms, and training rooms
Classrooms and monitored programming rooms in behavioral healthcare and correctional facilities
Lobbies and waiting areas
Police and fire stations
Explore Anchortex's Behavioral Healthcare Anti-Ligature Furniture and Prison and Detention Furniture collections for more institutional furniture.
[H2] About Norix Seating
Norix makes seating for behavioral healthcare, correctional, and other high-use facilities, from lightweight stackable chairs for staff areas to heavy, ballastable lounge seating for patient and inmate areas.
The Norix seating range includes:
Stackable Chairs: Integra, Progress, and Affinity
Guest and Lounge Seating: Flux, Forté, Vesta, Hondo Nuevo, Ripple, Wink, and Toro
Indoor and Outdoor Seating: Coupe, Flux, Pax, Kube, Goby, and Riptide
Upholstered Seating: Forma, Element, Harmony, and Respite
Rockers and Stools: Flux, Rocksmart, Mix-Up, and B-Side
Metal Seating: VersaFrame, Boulder, and Terra
[H2] About Norix Furniture
Norix manufactures durable furniture for demanding environments, including behavioral healthcare facilities, psychiatric hospitals, police stations, correctional institutions, and residential treatment centers. Explore the full line of Norix Furniture at Anchortex.

Notes and Questions
New series section: this batch has three seating products (Progress, Rocksmart, and Respite), so I wrote an "About Norix Seating" section based on the Norix Seating Guide (September 2026). It has no links to individual products. Please review it here; the same section will go on the Rocksmart and Respite tabs.
Norix use note: the spec sheet says "Ideal for staff use and monitored programming rooms. Not suitable for confined areas." I put this in the intro and wrote the applications for staff and supervised areas only.
Removed from the current page: "can be ordered as a sidechair, a linking sidechair or an armchair." The Norix spec sheet, web page, and price list show only the armless C920. Is there an arm or linking model?
Upholstery: the Norix web page says the chair comes "with or without upholstery" in 8 fabric grades, and 2 of the current photos show upholstered chairs, but the price list has no upholstered price and there is no upholstered variant. I listed it as an option. Should it stay?
TB133: our current page and the Norix Seating Guide both say the Progress Chair is not CAL TB133 compliant. I kept this as a bullet so buyers who need TB133 know. OK?
Price and weight checked: $181.60 = 80% of the Norix list price of $227 (compare-at $227). Weight 10 lbs matches the spec sheet and the worksheet (row 177: 10 / 23.2 / 19.7 / 32).
Images: the 5 current images are kept (alt text on all is "Norix C920 Progress Stackable Chair"). Norix also has plain photos of the chair in Twilight, Cove, Sand, and Dove. Would you like me to add the Twilight, Cove, and Dove photos (Sand is already on the page)?
Removed: the long old "About Norix Furniture" paragraph; replaced with the standard paragraph used on all Norix pages.
